title: TRACE: Diagnosing Verifier Brittleness in Agentic Evaluation
title_zh: TRACE：诊断智能体评测器的脆弱性
abstract_en: Verifier scores now serve as both benchmark metrics and training rewards for large language model (LLM) agents, and a change in score is routinely read as a change in capability. It may instead reflect a change in the evaluation. We introduce TRACE, a protocol that turns a score change from a verdict into a testable diagnosis: it applies a targeted change to one part of an evaluation, compares paired runs, checks whether the agent's behavior changed, and rescores unchanged trajectories to test whether the scoring rule is responsible. In a controlled suite of 25 synthetic tasks, renaming tools lowers a scripted agent's score by 0.250 even though it performs exactly the same operations; restoring the original names at scoring time closes the entire gap, while the same mutation exposes a genuine behavioral failure in a second agent. On public $τ^2$-bench tasks with four LLM agents, an initial 30-task study finds mixed reward changes whose one clear effect does not replicate. In a larger follow-up on 88 new tasks with repeated runs per condition, renaming tools or reformatting tool outputs leaves reward unchanged to within $\pm$0.10 for seven of eight agent-change pairs, whereas tool names that deliberately mislead lower every agent's reward by 0.20-0.44, showing that the setup can detect real effects. Identical reruns flip 15-36% of task outcomes, so single-run comparisons cannot separate presentation effects from run-to-run variation. Two frontier LLM judges give consistent verdicts when a fixed trajectory is presented differently, yet disagree with each other on 57% of the same records, largely because one grades procedure rather than outcome. TRACE thus separates what a score change says about the agent from what it says about the measurement.
abstract_zh: Verifier 分数既被用作大型语言模型（LLM）智能体的基准指标，也被用作训练奖励；但分数变化未必代表能力变化，也可能源于评测机制变化。论文提出 TRACE，一种将分数变化从“结论”转化为“可检验诊断”的协议：针对评测的某一部分进行定向修改，比较成对运行结果，检查智能体行为是否改变，并对未改变的轨迹重新评分，以判断问题是否来自评分规则。在包含 25 个合成任务的受控实验中，仅重命名工具就使脚本化智能体分数下降 0.250；在评分时恢复原工具名后，差距完全消失，而同样的修改又能暴露另一智能体的真实行为失败。在公开 τ^2-bench 任务上，初步 30 任务实验观察到混合的奖励变化，但唯一明显效应未能复现。随后对 88 个新任务进行多次重复实验发现，重命名工具或重新格式化工具输出，在 8 组智能体变化对中的 7 组使奖励变化保持在 ±0.10 以内；相反，故意误导性的工具名使所有智能体奖励下降 0.20–0.44，说明该协议能够检测真实影响。此外，相同条件的重复运行会导致 15%–36% 的任务结果翻转，因此单次运行无法区分展示效应与运行间随机波动。两名前沿 LLM 评审器在不同呈现方式下对固定轨迹的判断较一致，但对同一记录彼此有 57% 的分歧，主要因为其中一名更重视操作过程而非最终结果。TRACE 因而能够区分分数变化究竟反映了智能体本身，还是反映了测量方式。
key_points_zh: 提出 TRACE 诊断协议，通过定向修改评测、比较配对运行、检查行为变化并重评分原轨迹，定位分数变化来源。
在合成任务中，仅重命名工具就让脚本化智能体分数下降 0.250；恢复原名后差距完全消失，证明评测器可能产生伪变化。
在 88 个 τ^2-bench 新任务上，普通重命名或输出重格式化基本不影响奖励，而故意误导工具名会使所有智能体奖励下降 0.20–0.44，表明 TRACE 也能识别真实行为影响。
相同条件重复运行有 15%–36% 的任务结果翻转，说明单次运行无法可靠区分展示效应与随机波动。
不同 LLM 评审器对呈现变化较稳定，但彼此在 57% 的记录上意见不一致，分歧主要来自对过程与结果的不同偏好。

llm_assessment.comment: TRACE provides a rigorous reusable protocol for separating genuine agent behavior changes from verifier brittleness and evaluation noise.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: TRACE提供了严谨且可复用的协议，用于区分真实的智能体行为变化、验证器脆弱性与评测噪声。
